headline: 餵養獨裁者紀錄片登場
context: 紀錄片《How to Feed a Dictator》，訪問了曾為獨裁者掌廚的廚師，波布、伊迪．阿敏、海珊、皮諾契、金正日都在受訪者的服務名單上。畫面精緻的美食背後，對比的是這些政權下人民的飢餓。同一天，萊恩．墨菲（Ryan Murphy）改編布雷特．伊斯頓．艾利斯（Bret Easton Ellis）小說的新劇《The Shards》上線，評論認為這是他的回歸之作。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Andrew Neel’s documentary contrasts the lavish dishes eaten by heads of repressive states – served by largely unrepentant staff – with the starvation faced by their citizens There are moments in this sly documentary that evoke regular food porn, with crisply lit footage of vegetables being chopped and simmered, meat getting grilled, fat bubbling and browning – all the culinary sizzle is on display. Then there are climactic money shots, obligatory overhead views of the finished product, elegantly garnished, accompanied by text identifying the dish as, say, a Chilean country stew, or a whole roast goat, made precisely to suit the taste of a very specific client. It’s just that the clients these chefs served were despots, including Pol Pot, Idi Amin, Saddam Hussein, Augusto Pinochet and Kim Jong-il. Charles Otonde Odera once prepared a human heart “perfectly” for Amin, though at the time he thought better than to ask where the raw offal came from. Director Andrew Neel and editor Brad Turner skilfully weave together interviews with the chefs, each one in denial to varying degrees about their culpability in the repressive state apparatuses for which they worked. Odera in some ways is the most clear-eyed and honest, with Cambodian Keo Samoun coming in a very distant second, claiming she was just a kid (still in her teens) when she was recruited to cook for Pol Pot. Mind you, Samoun still brings a tasty spread of foodstuffs to her former employer’s grave to nourish his spirit. Meanwhile, Chilean cook Coco Pacheco is completely unrepentant, proud to have done his bit to tickle the palate of the man responsible for the torture and murder of thousands of his fellow countryman. Ermanno Furlanis, on the other hand, still just looks a bit baffled how he ended up making pizza for Kim Jong-il while millions of North Koreans starved. Continue reading...
sources.title: How to Feed a Dictator review – what was on the menu for some of the world’s most evil men

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Murphy is back on form with this gorgeously curated, shot and scored adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis’s novel – about a serial killer stalking privileged LA teenagers The world can finally begin to hope again. It looks as though Ryan Murphy has pulled out of his dive and is beginning to find his glorious groove again. The uber-showrunner reached a nadir last year with All’s Fair, a legal drama that was so bad it was existentially awful, garnering a number of rare, zero-star reviews ( including mine ) and which has duly been commissioned for a second series. But after All’s Fair came The Beauty . Which was chaotic and underdeveloped but fun. And then there was Love Story , about the short lives and love of JFK Jr and Carolyn Bessette, which was pitch-perfect, properly good trash. And now there is The Shards, Murphy’s adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis’s 80s-set metafictional/autobiographical novel of the same name. I have not read the book. An enfant terrible’s reminiscences are too often simply terrible and I was exhausted by the very idea. But a TV version? Run through the Murphytron? That sounds like a very good idea – and so it has proved. Theirs is a marriage made in pop-culture heaven. The Shards is on Disney+ Continue reading...

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Royal Opera House, London Mixing contemporary, Cuban and classical works, Acosta has charisma to burn and is accompanied by an impressive cohort It’s a bit of a stretch to call this undoubtedly enjoyable programme Myths and Modern Masters but granted, it sounds better than Miscellany. Carlos Acosta – superstar dancer, now director of Birmingham Royal Ballet and Cuban company Acosta Danza – has picked and mixed dancers from both companies to offer a very eclectic spread of dance, and added himself into the mix. At 53, Acosta may not have the physical prowess of his youth, but he brings great presence and depth – and some great dancing, too. That serves very well in José Limón’s landmark 1949 work The Moor’s Pavane, a distillation of Shakespeare’s Othello which boils down the story to four characters – Othello (Acosta), Desdemona (Beatrice Parma), Iago (Max Maslen) and Emilia (Miki Mizutani) – and contains their drama of deception, jealousy and revenge within a stately composition of measured steps and stylised gestures, set to courtly music by Purcell. thread_text:
紀錄片《How to Feed a Dictator》，訪問了曾為獨裁者掌廚的廚師，波布、伊迪．阿敏、海珊、皮諾契、金正日都在受訪者的服務名單上。畫面精緻的美食背後，對比的是這些政權下人民的飢餓。同一天，萊恩．墨菲（Ryan Murphy）改編布雷特．伊斯頓．艾利斯（Bret Easton Ellis）小說的新劇《The Shards》，在Disney+上線，評論認為這是墨菲的回歸之作。紐西蘭電影《Hunt for the Wilderpeople》也重新登上評論版面，被形容溫暖又聰明。倫敦皇家歌劇院，舞者卡洛斯．阿科斯塔（Carlos Acosta）帶來新作《Myths and Modern Masters》，融合當代、古巴與古典編舞；愛丁堡藝穗節，則有以鴉片類藥物危機為題材的新歌劇《The Galloping Cure》首演。

—— 本則整理自 The Guardian 的報導，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。
